title: Track and Tweak: Monitoring and Improving Group Fairness for Temporal Graph Neural Networks in Real Time

problem.claim: Temporal Graph Neural Networks can produce unfair outcomes across demographic groups in evolving systems.

gap.claim: Group fairness on temporal graphs had not been investigated, and existing fixed fairness regularization has critical limitations.

contributions.claim: The work proposes FTGNN-M, a monitoring-based approach that assesses fairness on the fly without relying on unseen test data.
FTGNN-M identifies embedding channels responsible for unfairness and adaptively adjusts the corresponding model parameters.
The approach provides theoretical guarantees for fairness assessment and fairness promotion.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first investigation of group fairness on temporal graphs and describe FTGNN-M as a new monitoring-based approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on five temporal transaction network datasets demonstrate effectiveness in utility and fairness metrics.
The authors report theoretical guarantees for fairness assessment and fairness promotion.

narrative_sequence.summary: Temporal networks and TGNNs create fairness challenges in evolving real-world applications.
The work introduces fixed fairness regularization through FTGNN-R, which operates in real time but has critical limitations.
FTGNN-M monitors fairness on the fly, identifies responsible embedding channels, and adaptively adjusts parameters.
The approach supports a fairness-utility trade-off and provides theoretical guarantees.
Experiments on five temporal transaction network datasets report effectiveness on utility and fairness metrics.

unknowns: The fairness definitions and demographic groups are not specified.
The limitations of FTGNN-R are not detailed.
The theoretical guarantee conditions and formal results are not provided.
